title: Parallel branches conflict on .slicer/log.jsonl and generated render/ files
findings_note: dogfooding: landing S60 onto main (which had S06) hit a log.jsonl merge conflict; generated .slicer/render/ files also conflict and must be re-rendered, not merged. Consider a union merge driver / .gitattributes for log.jsonl and a regenerate-on-merge story for render/.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Landing work on parallel branches conflicts on `.slicer/` files that should not need a
human merge. `log.jsonl` is append-only, so both sides just added different lines; `render/`
is a deterministic projection of `index.json`, so its "merge" is only a re-render. Only
`index.json` is the real source of truth whose overlaps are a genuine human job.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/cli.py: `cmd_init` writes `.slicer/.gitattributes`; `cmd_log` sorts by timestamp.
- src/slicer/store.py: `GITATTRIBUTES_NAME` constant.
- .slicer/.gitattributes: `log.jsonl merge=union`.
- README.md, docs/getting-started.md, docs/agents.md: the merge/rebase workflow.
- tests/test_merge.py: gitattributes, log ordering, and a real union merge.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
`slicer init` writes a `.slicer/.gitattributes` marking `log.jsonl merge=union`, so git's
built-in union driver combines both sides' appended history without a conflict (portable, no
per-clone config). `slicer log` sorts entries by timestamp (newest first, later-appended
breaking ties) so union-interleaved lines still read in order. Document that `render/` is
regenerated after a merge (resolve `index.json`, `slicer render`), leaning on the existing
`slicer check` staleness gate.

A custom git merge driver that auto-regenerates `render/` was considered and deferred: it
needs per-clone `git config` and crosses slicer's "never writes git" boundary to automate a
one-command fix in an occasional case. Revisit if `render/` conflicts prove frequent.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run the focused merge tests, the unit suite, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`. Manually
confirm in a throwaway git repo that two branches each running a `slicer` mutation merge with
no conflict in `log.jsonl`.
